title: NUMA-aware copy coalescer and adaptive kernel picker to cut host stalls
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce host-side CPU and scheduling overhead in the prefill->decode pipeline for small-to-medium batch workloads by (1) coalescing and aligning host->GPU memory transfers with NUMA locality, (2) introducing a low-overhead adaptive kernel selection path that picks the best kernel variant for the current (model, seq_len, batch) slice, and (3) pacing prefill/decoder work to avoid threadpool contention and frequent short-lived memcpy submissions.

Background: Recent production traces show a high rate of tiny host->device memcpy submissions and many short-lived worker threads contending on the CPU threadpool during mixed-latency workloads (chat + background embeddings). This causes tail latency spikes and inflated host CPU for small batches (1-8). Kernel selection currently uses a static mapping that doesn't adapt to runtime seq_len distributions and attention-type (causal vs. bi-attn), so we sometimes run suboptimal kernels that increase computation time on GPU and force more frequent KV flushes.

Proposal: Implement three coordinated changes: 
1) NUMA-aware copy coalescer: a lightweight coalescer that runs per-NUMA-node and batches small memcpy requests into page-aligned, contiguous transfers using a per-NUMA pinned buffer pool. The coalescer will expose a non-blocking enqueue API used by the host pipeline. A single DMA submission worker per NUMA node will drain coalesced entries, reducing syscall and PCIe submission churn. Use heuristics for flush thresholds (time and size) to trade latency vs coalescing efficiency.

2) Adaptive kernel picker: add a micro-benchmarking probe that runs inexpensive runtimes (warmup <= 2 steps) of candidate kernel variants for specific (model shard, sequence length bucket, batch size). The runtime will maintain a tiny LRU cache of best-variant decisions keyed by (model-id, seq_bucket, attention_mode). The picker must be non-blocking and fall back to the static default on cold-starts or when probes are throttled. Keep probing rate low and correlated with traffic patterns.

3) Prefill/Decode pacing and single-producer scheduling: decouple prefill work submission from decode via a token-window pacing algorithm that restricts the number of inflight small tasks created simultaneously. Replace multiple short-lived tasks that race on the threadpool with an ordered single-producer queue per-device that owns DMA/coalesce submission; workers pull work for decode once a token window is available. This reduces mutex contention and context switching on the host.

Metrics and success criteria are listed below; implementation will be staged: feature-flag the coalescer first, then kernel-picker, then pacing. Provide a runtime flag to force coalescing off for debugging.

Compatibility notes: ensure pinned-buffer pool works with our existing memory allocator and is cleaned up on model unload. Kernel picker must be conservative for quantized kernels (int8/int4) because throughput profiles can vary with batch packing.

Observability: add counters for coalesced_bytes, coalesced_calls, dma_flushes, kernel_probe_hits/misses, average_probe-latency, per-numa CPU utilization, host memcpy syscall rate, threadpool queue length. Expose rollout dashboard in Console under runtime-1.20 experiments.
acceptance_criteria: Host CPU utilization (system + user) for mixed chat workload (1-8 batch) reduced by >=30% in steady-state compared to baseline
Number of host memcpy syscall submissions reduced by >=60% for the target workload
P95 tail latency for small-batch decode reduced by >=15% without regressions on p50
Kernel picker must demonstrate >5% GPU time improvement for at least two representative open-models on test harness
Feature gated and toggles available; safe rollback path and metrics dashboard live
benchmarks: 2025-02-24 microbench (local): small-batch chat (batch=1-4) -> host CPU -42%, memcpy-calls -68%, tokens/sec +6% (prototype coalescer enabled)
2025-02-28 lab run: kernel probe on mix-model workload -> median GPU kernel time -7% for attentional-path, p95 unchanged (safe fallback engaged)
risks: Coalescer flush thresholds may increase  p50 unless tuned per-workload; must tune in canary
Pinned buffer pool increases host memory pressure for heavy multi-tenant hosts; need eviction policy
Kernel probing could pick unstable kernels for quantized paths if probes are too sparse
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Feature-flagged NUMA coalescer behind canary (10% of traffic) for two weeks; monitor host CPU, memcpy rate, and latency dashboards
Stage 2: Enable adaptive kernel picker in lab and then canary 5% traffic; keep static mapping as fallback
Stage 3: Enable pacing/producer queue with conservative token window in canary; evaluate threadpool contention metrics
Stage 4: Gradual ramp to 100% with rollback toggles and automated anomaly detection on latency and throughput
comments: 2025-02-16 Asha Patel: Spiked the idea in runtime sync; agreed this addresses both syscall churn and thread contention. Assigned to Diego.
2025-02-20 Diego Morales: Prototype NUMA coalescer implemented (see PR). Initial local bench shows promising drop in memcpy calls. Still instrumenting pinned pool memory usage.

2025-02-24 Linus Kwan (review): Reviewed coalescer PR - suggested making page-alignment optional for tiny transfers to avoid copy inflation. Also asked for metrics to indicate when coalescing added >1ms latency.

2025-02-25 Diego Morales: Added probe harness for adaptive kernel picker; microbench shows kernel swap reduces kernel time by ~10% for seq=512 on model-x. Need to add safety thresholds for quantized kernels.

2025-03-01 Sara Goldberg (perf): Ran lab mix-model job. Coalescer + pacing reduced host CPU by ~35% and lowered p95 by 18% for the target scenario. Noticed higher RSS on heavy-host nodes; adding eviction and per-host caps.
2025-03-03 Diego Morales: Merging coalescer to canary branch  -- enabling 10% traffic next week. Kernel picker still behind flag; will start canary probes after canary stabilizes.
